paragraphs.text: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities affecting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, while a critical ASP.NET library flaw and a GL.iNet cloud management compromise demonstrate widespread exploitation of software supply chain and vendor-managed services. These developments require immediate asset inventory and remediation tracking across multiple technology stacks. Vulnerability management owners must confirm coverage for each affected product and validate compensating controls where patching is delayed.

A payment processor breach exposed credit card numbers and CVVs at Cleverbridge, AI-assisted attacks triggered unauthorized transactions at Indian financial institutions, and a cryptographic library flaw in GPGME permits data theft through malicious keys. These events highlight expanding third-party risk, evolving fraud techniques, and foundational library vulnerabilities affecting data protection. Data protection and third-party risk owners should review supplier assurance for cardholder data, enhance monitoring for AI-driven anomalies, and inventory GPGME dependencies.
